title: Live storm updates: Waterspouts spotted over San Francisco Bay amid severe weather
text:
Live Bay Area storm updates: Waterspouts spotted over San Francisco Bay amid severe weather - ABC7 San Francisco 
 24/7 Live San Francisco East Bay South Bay Peninsula North Bay Live WEATHER 
 Live storm updates: Waterspouts spotted over San Francisco Bay amid severe weather 
 Stream local breaking news and original programming, live 24/7, from ABC7 Bay Area. By ABC7 Bay Area Digital Staff Last updated: Monday, November 16, 2026 10:03PM GMT Share Follow ABC7 on Google A series of storms will bring heavy rain, flash flooding, gusty winds and possible debris flows to the San Francisco Bay Area over the next week.
 According to ABC7 Eyewitness News meteorologist Drew Tuma, this is a strong Level 2 storm on the ABC7 Exclusive Storm Impact Scale and could be bumped up to a Level 3 as it nears the region.
 LIVE: Track rain in San Francisco Bay Area with Live Doppler 7 
 In a forecast briefing released before 4 a.m. Monday, the weather service projected that the next system is expected to arrive Tuesday night and continue into early Friday morning, with the greatest impacts forecast for Wednesday and Thursday. Rain could linger across the region through the weekend.
 Moderate to heavy rainfall could cause minor flooding, while areas affected by recent wildfires face a higher risk of flash flooding, mud and debris flows. Some roads could become impassable because of flooding or damage, forecasters warned.

 Key Headlines
 52 minutes ago Waterspouts spotted over SF Bay amid severe weather 
 58 minutes ago Tornado Warning canceled after being issued for Santa Cruz County 
 6:30 PM GMT VIDEO: Scary moments surfers were rescued from rough waves off Santa Cruz 
 4:00 PM GMT Huge waves pummel the California coast, forcing the closure of iconic piers 
 Here's how the news is developing. 52 minutes ago 
 Waterspouts spotted over SF Bay amid severe weather 
 Massive waterspouts were spotted Monday dancing on the San Francisco Bay as severe weather moved through the Bay Area.
 In several photos and videos circulating on social media, tall waterspouts can be seen going high into the clouds.
 Viewers have sent photos and videos to ABC7 Eyewitness News of waterspouts being seen from San Francisco, Daly City, and other locations around the Bay.
 Waterspout seen from San Francisco. Waterspout seen from Daly City over the San Francisco Bay. This comes as a Tornado Warning was issued for parts of Santa Cruz County.
 58 minutes ago 
 Tornado Warning canceled after being issued for Santa Cruz County 
 The National Weather Service has canceled a Tornado Warning that was issued in Santa Cruz County on Monday afternoon.
 The NWS had the warning in effect until 1:30 p.m.
 Elsewhere, there have been reports of waterspouts on the San Francisco Bay.
 By Gloria Rodríguez 3 hours and 38 minutes ago 
 High surf continues to wallop Pacifica, where residents are impacted by flooded streets 
 Massive waves continued to pound the Bay Area coastline Monday, causing flooding and sand buildup on roads near the Pacifica Pier as crews worked to clear affected areas. Massive waves continued to pound the Bay Area coastline Monday, causing flooding and sand buildup on roads near the Pacifica Pier as crews worked to clear affected areas.
 Roads around the pier that were flooded are now covered in sand, creating travel challenges for residents. Throughout Monday morning, waves splashed over barricades and onto sidewalks, causing ponding on nearby roads.
 The Pacifica Pier has taken a beating from high surf over the weekend and Monday. Crews have already been working to shore up the pier, which has experienced cracking. A café on the pier was previously demolished.
 Residents said the impacts from the weekend storm have made it more difficult to get around the area.
 "A lot of these streets are one-way. So for us to get to our homes, we can't, like, drive. We weren't able to drive through Beach Boulevard. And so it's more of just like a kind of an inconvenience right now because my home isn't on Beach Boulevard. So like, walking my dog, for example, I have to walk all the way around or like, I can't drive through here," said Carla Paredes, a Pacifica resident.
 Nearby at Rockaway Beach, intense waves also battered the shoreline, narrowly missing cars in the parking lot near Nick's Rockaway restaurant.
 Crews continued working near the pier Monday as dangerous surf conditions persisted along the coast.
 6:30 PM GMT 
 VIDEO: Scary moments surfers were rescued from rough waves off Santa Cruz 
 Three surfers were pulled from the intense swells in Santa Cruz by a rescuer on a jet ski, but things got scary when they got hit by a wave that overturned the jet ski and sent them flying back into the water. Three surfers were rescued Saturday near Pleasure Point in Santa Cruz during a challenging operation complicated by high tides, kelp and swells, according to Santa Cruz fire officials.
 A fire department rescuer on a jet ski pulled two surfers from the water Saturday off the coast near Pleasure Point. Santa Cruz fire officials said kelp and swells made the rescue effort more difficult.
 Witness Paige Gordon described a dramatic moment during the rescue when they all got knocked off the jet ski. The rescuer recovered after the jet ski overturned and completed the rescue operation.
 "Unfortunately, a big wave barrelled into them, and it threw the jet ski over and everyone went flying," Gordon said. "And then everyone started screaming. I started crying; it's hard to watch something like that, especially when you see someone like a first responder trying to help people. And I don't know how jet skis work so I didn't know if it was gonna sink or what was happening. But luckily the guy got it back over. I've never seen something like that in real life, what a professional."
 About 10 minutes later, the rescuer returned and helped another surfer out of the water.
 No additional information about the surfers or their conditions was released.
